newsitem.title: CHINA: China car market stalling, inventories rise.
newsitem.headline: China car market stalling, inventories rise.

text.p: China's car market is in the doldrums because of overproduction, fierce competition, poor roads and local protectionism, the official media and salesmen said Thursday.
"We have 15,000 cars in stock, higher than the usual level," said a salesman for Shanghai Automobile Industry Group (SAIG) which sells China's top passenger car, the Santana.
Output of the Santana, a joint venture with Germany's Volkswagen AG, is due to reach 200,000 this year, up from 160,000 in 1995.

"The inventory situation of other manufacturers is worse than ours," he said. "The domestic market is weak because of oversupply, too many imports, protectionism by local governments aimed at keeping out Santanas and a chaotic market."

In 1995, China produced 1.5 million vehicles, up 10 percent from 1994. It is expected to produce 2.7 million in 2000. China's vehicle output in the first half of 1996 was 758,000, official figures show.
The Shanghai-based Business News said China's auto industry suffered badly in the first half of 1996, with serious losses in June and July.
It blamed an excess of imported cars, a serious shortage of roads, the negative impact of the auto industry on the environment and a shortage of capital.
